rationale: This is a cosmetic tightening of the archived "R&D-Backed Pricing Power" signal — it merely appends a third MIN conjunct (MA(xrd/sale,3)) that is highly correlated with the existing R&D-share term, so it is unlikely to deliver information beyond the already-tested version whose portfolio evidence was weak (ls_talpha 1.14).

Because cumulative R&D is slow-moving, the first difference of xrd_sum/(che+xrd_sum) is mechanically dominated by changes in cash holdings, making this largely a rediscovery of the known change-in-cash/cash-holdings anomaly rather than an R&D-financing interaction, and the expected negative sign also sits awkwardly against the archived level version's strongly positive fmb_tstat (+4.63).

Replacing the maturity share with a short-debt-versus-cash liquidity measure is a defensible economic re-specification rather than a pure re-scaling of the archived maturity-mismatch signal, though it remains close to well-documented distress/liquidity interactions and the earlier variant's evidence was marginal.

This is a post-hoc sign flip of the archived "R&D Capital-Renewal Shortfall" (whose fmb and alpha both came out positive) with a third conjunct borrowed from another archived signal, so it is a hybrid re-labelling fitted to prior results rather than a new mechanism, and the triple MIN further shrinks effective breadth in an already thin sample.

Converting the goodwill/productivity bottleneck into a signed product genuinely changes the portfolio construction by making zero-goodwill firms neutral rather than the short leg, which is a substantive fix, though a large tie mass at exactly zero will compress the ranking and dilute both tails.

The lagged-acquisition-then-R&D-decline sequencing is a coherent and reasonably novel crowding-out test, but the long leg will be dominated by zero-aqc firms, so much of the spread risks being the well-known acquirer-underperformance/asset-growth anomaly rather than the proposed interaction.
